# ADR-046a — Amendment to ADR-046: authoritative zero-bucket daily densification permitted, insert-only, still clamped

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Amendment to ADR-046 (2026-08-25, Checkpoint 6.3, user-approved): authoritative zero-bucket daily densification is permitted.** ADR-046's blanket rule -- densification "is skipped entirely when a chunk returns zero buckets" -- was written in Checkpoint 6.0, when nothing could distinguish an authoritatively-empty window from a transiently-empty one. Checkpoint 6.3's authority model can: `authoritative = fetchComplete && rejections === 0 && kind !== 'hot'`. A **fully fetched, rejection-free, non-hot daily window returning zero buckets may therefore create verified-absence rows** (`has_data = false`). Strictly bounded: those writes are **insert-only** and may never overwrite or downgrade an existing `has_data = true` row; they remain clamped by `first_data_date` at the start and `lastGloballyCompleteDateExclusive(now)` at the end, so neither pre-device history nor a still-in-flight civil day can be stamped verified-absent; an incomplete, rejected, `hot` or otherwise non-authoritative empty response writes **nothing**; and later real data may replace a `has_data = false` marker. **This amendment applies only to daily-metric densification.** An empty session key set still cannot trigger tombstoning (ADR-047a) -- `x <> ALL('{}'::text[])` is TRUE in Postgres, so an ungated empty sweep would tombstone an entire window. Everything else in ADR-046 -- the trailing-window re-fetch, the 35-day staleness contract, the permanent webhook exclusion -- is unchanged
